title: The Gaussian moat problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Walks through Gaussian primes with bounded steps. The arithmetic of split primes and the reduction of the uniform component bound to a finite periodic sieve; Shannon entropy, Pinsker's inequality, short lists of candidates and averages over random coordinates; Hoeffding's inequality and the isoperimetry of the discrete cube; many differences of a walk stretch and their separation by randomly signed products of Gaussian primes; entropy enrichment by sampling differences; coverage transferred backwards with shared continuations; a common sampling schedule; and the information cost of avoiding zero classes. Together they prove that for every step bound the connected components of the Gaussian-prime graph have bounded size, so that one cannot walk to infinity on Gaussian primes with bounded steps.
prerequisites: Core course C40 (Euclidean domains, unique factorization)
Core course D60, Lecture 30 (Brouwer's fixed-point theorem)
NT-DIRL lesson on the prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions
